monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: db.m6i.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: cache.t4g.medium — AWS ElastiCache us-east-1 / On-Demand / Redis engine / standard support / 730 h per month; node-hour only. Band: zero-width at the Redis/Memcached standard-support rate. The Valkey engine is CHEAPER and Extended Support is DEARER; both are different products/support states, not a price range for this row, so they are named here rather than used as band edges.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 5,000 operations/s at peak, counted as 1,500 submits/s + 1,500 executions/s + 2,000 status polls/s. One job is TWO operations here (an enqueue and a dequeue), because the engine is a synchronous open queueing network and the only honest way to charge a worker for its share of load is to give the consume side its own flow.

assumptions.subject: execute
assumptions.statement: The 'execute' flow's latency is worker SERVICE time, not end-to-end job completion. Time a job spends WAITING in the broker before a worker picks it up is not modelled — the v1 analytical engine has no backlog/queue-depth model, so a deep backlog would not show up as latency here.

assumptions.subject: worker
assumptions.statement: Workers are sized at ~200 jobs/s each with a ~40 ms mean job (about 8 concurrent jobs per instance). This is the input most worth replacing with your own measurement — job cost varies by orders of magnitude, and the workers are the bottleneck in this design.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Status polls hit a Redis cache with an assumed 85% hit rate (db visit_prob 0.15) — a polled job's state is read far more often than it changes.

assumptions.subject: store
assumptions.statement: 20% of submissions carry a payload too large to inline, and 30% of executions write a result blob. Small payloads/results ride in the job row.

assumptions.subject: q
assumptions.statement: 3 brokers is the durability floor (replication factor 3), not a throughput requirement — the cluster sits far below its rps ceiling on purpose. Sizing a broker cluster by rps alone would under-provision partitions and retention.

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: One Postgres primary, no standby modelled. An HA standby serves no traffic, so adding it as a second instance would falsely DOUBLE the engine's capacity for this component. The single-instance SPOF is real and is flagged as such.

assumptions.subject: retries
assumptions.statement: Retries and a dead-letter queue are REQUIRED in a real task queue and are NOT in this model: the engine has no failure/retry model, so a retry storm (the classic task-queue outage) cannot be simulated here.

_library.summary: Submit work over an API, run it on a worker fleet behind a durable broker, and poll the job's status.
